summary: Tested the two new additive features (admin lead delete + Google Search Console verification meta) plus regressions. Backend: 41/41 pytest tests pass including a new suite /app/backend/tests/test_lead_delete_and_gsc.py (DELETE /api/leads/{id} -> {ok:true}, 404 for unknown id, 404 on double delete, 401 without admin JWT, removal verified via GET /api/leads; seo.google_verification present in GET /api/settings, persists after PUT /api/admin/settings/site and restores to ''). Frontend: admin login at /admin works, Leads Dashboard + expanded site-settings panel render, per-row delete button data-testid lead-delete-<id> found for an API-created lead, window.confirm ('Delete this lead permanently? This cannot be undone.') accepted, row disappeared and lead gone from API. settings-seo-google_verification field accepted 'test-gsc-verify-123', site-settings-save showed 'Site settings saved' toast, GET /api/settings returned the value, and the public homepage DOM head contained <meta name="google-site-verification" content="test-gsc-verify-123">. Homepage renders with no 'Compiled with problems' overlay and no webpack overlay iframe; marketing.popup_enabled toggle persistence verified by backend test. DB left in default state: seo.google_verification reset to '', marketing reset to {offers_enabled:true, popup_enabled:true, offers_end_date:''}, and all 17 stale TEST_ leads deleted via the new endpoint (0 TEST_ leads remaining).

ui_bugs.issue: Pre-existing React console error persists on /admin: 'In HTML, <span> cannot be a child of <option> ... will cause a hydration error'. Cosmetic only.

issues: 'Auto-turn-off date' uses the browser-native date input (mm/dd/yyyy) rather than a shadcn Calendar/date-picker component - inconsistent with the rest of the UI (pre-existing, low priority)

action_items: Optional/low: remove the <span> rendered inside a native <option> in Admin.jsx to clear the React hydration console error.
Optional/low: replace the native date input for 'Auto-turn-off date' with the shadcn calendar component.
critical_code_review_comments: DELETE /api/leads/{lead_id} is correctly admin-guarded and returns 404 when deleted_count == 0 - no soft-delete/audit trail, so deletion is irreversible; acceptable for spam cleanup but consider archiving if lead history matters.
SiteSettings.save() still PUTs the entire settings document (including seo.google_verification); concurrent admin edits can clobber each other. Fine for single-admin use.

Seo.jsx conditionally emits the google-site-verification meta only when non-empty - correct; note the tag is client-rendered, so verification relies on Emergent's crawler-prerender layer for Googlebot HTML-tag verification (DNS/HTML-file method may be safer if GSC verification fails).
